# 03b One name for a style target, and one declaration-list parser

## Outcome

`StyleDecl` names its targets `targetIds`, and the code that splits an author's
`fill:#fdd,stroke:#c00` into properties exists once instead of once per parser.

## Why this ticket exists

Two loose ends, both spanning both parser files, both created by this board and both due to land
before ticket 04 makes them worse.

**The name.** `StyleDecl.classIds` now holds flowchart node ids. `resolveStyles.ts:75` already reads
`for (const targetId of declaration.classIds)` — the misreading in one line. Ticket 01b renamed
every other style type; this field was missed by the board's rename table, and tickets 01 and 03
were each denied the files needed to fix it. That was the planner's error twice over, not a
worker's.

**The parser.** `splitDeclarations` and `parseStyleProperties` now exist character-for-character in
both `parseFlowchart.ts` (:40, :73) and `parseClassDiagram.ts` (:153, :185). Ticket 03's worker
created the second copy knowingly and flagged it, because neither the target file nor a new module
was in its scope. Ticket 04 gives flowchart `classDef` and `class`, which is where a third caller
of the same splitting rules appears — the exact shape board 2 spent four tickets undoing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `StyleDecl.classIds` → `targetIds`, everywhere. `tsc --noEmit` finds every site; grep to prove
      none survives. The doc comment moves with it and stops saying "classes".
- [x] No test assertion changes **value**. This is a field rename, so the same discipline ticket 01b
      used applies: make it checkable that the edits are vocabulary only, and say in your report how.
      A purely mechanical substitution is the evidence — ticket 01b's script-and-diff is the
      precedent, take it or do something equally checkable.
- [x] `splitDeclarations` and `parseStyleProperties` live in one module both parsers import.
      Name it for what it parses. Neither parser retains a copy.
- [x] **Check whether the two copies are actually identical before merging them.** Ticket 03's
      worker said "character for character", but verify it by diff rather than inheriting the claim
      — a behavioral difference silently unified is the failure mode board 2 hit with the timeline
      drain, and it cost a whole ticket to discover.
- [x] Every existing parser test passes **unedited** in both kinds. This is behavior-preserving.
- [x] The malformed-declaration diagnostic (`Unrecognized style declaration: "oops"`) stays
      identical for both kinds, including line and column.

## Test seam

The two parsers through their source strings, as they are tested today, plus the shared module
directly if the extraction earns its own tests.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Ticket 03b: prove every edit to a test suite is vocabulary only.

Reads a pre-ticket file on stdin (`git show 2033dc7:<path>`) and writes it
back out with ONLY the two rewrites below applied. Nothing else in this
script can change a byte, so if its output is byte-identical to the
working-tree file, this ticket's edit to that suite is exactly these
rewrites: no assertion's meaning moved, nothing was added, removed or
reordered, and every diagnostic string, ordering claim and gate rejection is
the one that was already asserted.

  for f in packages/core/src/graph-model/buildClassModel.test.ts \
           packages/core/src/graph-model/buildGraphModel.test.ts \
           packages/core/src/graph-model/resolveStyles.test.ts \
           packages/core/src/index.test.ts \
           packages/core/src/layout/layoutClassDiagram.test.ts \
           packages/core/src/parser/parseClassDiagram.test.ts \
           packages/core/src/parser/parseSiren.test.ts; do
    git show 2033dc7:$f | python3 .scratch/siren-author-styling-slice/03b-vocabulary-only.py \
      | diff - $f && echo "OK $f"
  done

`classIds` names two different things in this package, exactly as `classId`
did for ticket 01b:

  * `StyleDecl.classIds` — the ids a `style`/apply-directive targets. Since
    ticket 03 those are flowchart node ids as often as class ids. THIS is
    what the ticket renames to `targetIds`.
  * `ClassNamespace.classIds` and `ResolvedClassNamespace.classIds` — the
    member classes of a `namespace Foo { }` block. Genuinely classes, and
    untouched.

The two rules below are written to separate them by shape alone, so the
separation can be read rather than trusted:

(1) A line that is nothing but a `classIds:` field whose value opens an
    array literal. Every `StyleDecl` fixture in these suites is spelled that
    way (ticket 01b's added field pushed them all onto their own lines). No
    namespace fixture is: a namespace literal always carries its `id:` on
    the same line (`{ id: "BaseShapes", classIds: ["Triangle"] }`), and
    `layoutClassDiagram.test.ts`'s namespace helper declares the parameter
    as `classIds: string[],`, whose value is not an array literal.

(2) A line that also carries `styleKind:`, which only a `StyleDecl` literal
    ever does. This catches the one style fixture still written inline,
    `resolveStyles.test.ts`'s `styleDecl({ styleKind: "style", classIds: ...`.

Every other appearance of the word — a `const classIds =` local in
`index.test.ts`, a `model!.namespaces[0].classIds` read, a namespace literal
— matches neither rule and is passed through unchanged.
"""

import re
import sys

STANDALONE_FIELD_RE = re.compile(r'^(\s*)classIds: (\[.*)$')


def main() -> None:
    out = []
    for line in sys.stdin.read().split('\n'):
        field = STANDALONE_FIELD_RE.match(line)
        if field is not None:
            indent, value = field.groups()
            out.append(f'{indent}targetIds: {value}')
            continue

        if 'styleKind:' in line:
            line = line.replace('classIds:', 'targetIds:')
        out.append(line)

    sys.stdout.write('\n'.join(out))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```
